title: Objectives, Revenues, Costs and Profits: assessment

questions.q: For a firm facing a downward-sloping demand curve, MR is:
questions.ok: Correct: Price must fall on all units to sell more, so MR lies below AR.
questions.fb: Price must fall on all units to sell more, so MR lies below AR. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: Total revenue is at its maximum where:
questions.ok: Correct: When MR is zero, extra sales add nothing to revenue.
questions.fb: When MR is zero, extra sales add nothing to revenue. Review the Learn tab.
MC = MR. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: Where MR is positive, demand is:
questions.ok: Correct: A price cut raises revenue only if demand is elastic.
questions.fb: A price cut raises revenue only if demand is elastic. Review the Learn tab.

questions.ok: Correct: MC passes through the minimum of AC.
questions.fb: MC passes through the minimum of AC. Review the Learn tab.

questions.ok: Correct: Normal profit is the minimum to keep the firm in the industry.
questions.fb: Normal profit is the minimum to keep the firm in the industry. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: Sales maximisation (with no loss) occurs where:
questions.ok: Correct: Output is pushed as far as AR = AC.
questions.fb: Output is pushed as far as AR = AC. Review the Learn tab.

questions.q: A firm sells 40 units at £15 each. Calculate total revenue (£).
questions.fb: TR = P × Q = 15 × 40 = £600. Check the worked examples.

questions.q: Total cost is £480 for 40 units. Calculate average cost (£).
questions.fb: AC = TC ÷ Q = 480 ÷ 40 = £12. Check the worked examples.

questions.q: TR rises from £600 to £660 when output rises from 40 to 44 units. Calculate marginal revenue (£).
questions.fb: MR = ΔTR ÷ ΔQ = 60 ÷ 4 = £15. Check the worked examples.
